evidence: provider documentation and crit-labs' own source; calls, formats and GPUs are as the providers state them, not measured by crit unless a kernel says so

operations.what: rows times NVFP4 weights (E2M1 codes, E4M3 scale per 16, one global scale): decode GEMVs with 16-bit activations, prompt GEMMs with 16-bit or NVFP4 activations
operations.verify: on the target, project a few rows of a real matrix with the kernel and with project (FP64): within FP16/BF16 accumulation error for 16-bit activations; with NVFP4 activations compare against project of the activations quantized by quantize_row, then judge the drift with crit eval's quality run. Same bits on a repeat

kernels.call: cublasLtMatmul with A and B of type CUDA_R_4F_E2M1 and CUBLASLT_MATMUL_MATRIX_SCALE_VEC16_UE4M3 as both operands' scale mode (CUDA 12.8 and newer); the global scales fold into alpha
kernels.shapes: prompt GEMMs; K a multiple of the scale block, N and K aligned as cuBLASLt's block-scaled GEMM requires
kernels.scale_layout: the block scales of both operands in cuBLASLt's tiled block-scaling layout (128 x 4 tiles), not row-major: repack the weights' scales once at load and quantize activations straight into it

kernels.call: CUTLASS's block-scaled GEMM for sm_100 / sm_120 (NVFP4 x NVFP4), or a mixed-input GEMM that widens the 4-bit weights inside the main loop for 16-bit activations
formats: nvfp4 weights with bf16 or fp16 activations (mixed input)
kernels.shapes: aligned as the chosen tile requires

operations.what: 16-bit activation rows to NVFP4 with the checkpoint's global input scale: E4M3 block scale e4m3(amax / 6 * gs) and E2M1 codes per 16, each row on its own
operations.verify: on the target, quantize a few real activation rows with the kernel and with quantize_row at the same global scale: identical codes and scale bytes once the kernel's scale layout is unswizzled, and the same bits on a repeat

kernels.call: flashinfer's fp4_quantize(input, global_scale, ...) with its swizzled scale-factor layout, the layout cuBLASLt's block-scaled GEMM reads
formats: bf16 or fp16 in, nvfp4 out
archs: sm_120 (where the FlashInfer release builds it)
kernels.scale_layout: swizzled 128 x 4 tiles when its swizzle option is on; row-major otherwise

operations.what: rows times FP8 E4M3 weights with one scale per row (and per-token FP8 activations for prompts)
operations.verify: on the target, project a few rows with the kernel and with the double-accumulating oracle: within FP32 accumulation error of the scaled products, the same bits on a repeat

kernels.call: torch._scaled_mm(a_fp8, b_fp8, scale_a, scale_b, out_dtype=...) with row-wise scales (scale_a [M, 1], scale_b [1, N])
formats: fp8_e4m3 x fp8_e4m3 with row-wise scales
archs: sm_89 and newer (row-wise scaling on sm_90 and newer)

kernels.call: cublasLtMatmul with CUDA_R_8F_E4M3 operands and per-tensor scale pointers (CUBLASLT_MATMUL_DESC_A_SCALE_POINTER, ..._B_SCALE_POINTER); row scales through an outer-vector scale mode where the toolkit and GPU support it, else an epilogue
kernels.shapes: aligned as cuBLASLt's FP8 GEMM requires (multiples of 16)
